candidates.title: Design doc's §7.5 step 5 "archive commit is the run's last one" invariant is now false, and no task in the plan is scoped to fix it
candidates.detail: §7.5 step 5 states "commit `takt(<slug>): archive`. That commit is the run's last one, which is what lets a merge carry the archived bundle" (lines 884-885), and describes the only mechanism by which the bundle directory can still change post-archive as a later `next` sweeping dirty files into a *second archive commit* (lines 902-911: "the bundle directory is otherwise untouched once archived"). This diff's `finishOrArchivedOnly` lets `done --step retro` run in the `archived` phase and, per the new `doneRetro` doc comment (internal/cli/cmd_done.go:189-191) and TestDoneRetroAcceptedInArchivedPhase, produce its own ordinary `"retro done"` bundle commit landing after the archive commit — a distinct mechanism the design doc doesn't describe, and one that falsifies the "last one" claim outright for the `keep` disposition. Task 8 (the dedicated docs task for this section) explicitly scopes its edits, and its own verify checks, to only the `3. **Retro**`–`4. **Disposition**` markers of step 3 (docs/takt/lets-work-on-63/plan.md:92-97), so step 5's stale text is left unaddressed by the plan as written.

candidates.title: Redundant []byte→string conversions in unfilledProseSlot
candidates.detail: unfilledProseSlot converts b to a string twice (line 49 `strings.Index(string(b), marker)` and line 53 `rest := string(b)[i:]`), each allocating a full copy of retro.md's contents. bytes.Index (already available without adding an import beyond "bytes") or a single `s := string(b)` at the top would avoid the duplicate conversion. Retro.md is small so this has no real cost, but it's an easy simplification the diff didn't take.

candidates.title: os.ReadFile error path in doneRetro untested
candidates.detail: The new `b, err := os.ReadFile(p)` after the fileNonEmpty(p) check has no test forcing a read failure (e.g. permission denied) between the existence check and the read, so the new `fail(...)` branch at line 203 is never hit. This mirrors an existing untested pattern elsewhere in the file (e.g. doneGoals), so it's a pre-existing convention rather than a new regression, but it is new code added by this diff with zero coverage.

candidates.title: unfilledProseSlot's unterminated-marker branch is never exercised
candidates.detail: unfilledProseSlot has two return paths when a marker is found: one where a closing `-->` exists (tested by TestDoneRetroRefusesUnfilledProseSlot) and one where it's missing (`j < 0`, returns `rest, true` — the whole tail of the file as the 'slot'). No test writes a retro.md with a `<!-- prose:` marker lacking a closing `-->`, so this branch, and the resulting (arguably surprising) full-tail error message, is unverified.

candidates.title: Doc comment reads awkwardly where it cross-references the new helper
candidates.detail: The updated finishPhaseOnly doc comment says "Both refuse in the one shape finishOrArchivedOnly also uses for `done --step retro`, so a session learns it once" — missing a connective (e.g. "the one shape that finishOrArchivedOnly also uses"), making the two sibling doc comments (finishPhaseOnly at line 44 and finishOrArchivedOnly at line 60) harder to read together as the single explanation they're meant to be.

candidates.title: "finish or archived" predicate duplicated instead of shared
candidates.detail: finishOrArchivedOnly (cmd_verify.go:65) hardcodes `st.Phase == bundle.PhaseFinish || st.Phase == bundle.PhaseArchived`, which is exactly the boolean already inlined at internal/cli/cmd_status.go:154 (`if st.Phase == bundle.PhaseFinish || st.Phase == bundle.PhaseArchived`). The diff had a natural opportunity to factor this into a shared predicate (e.g. a small `finishOrArchived(st) bool` used by both the gate function and cmd_status.go) instead of adding a second independent encoding of the same phase-pair rule.

verdicts.evidence: Design doc §7.5 step 5 states the archive commit 'is the run's last one' (line 884) and that 'there is no write after the archive commit' / 'the bundle directory is otherwise untouched once archived' (lines 902-909), describing only a second *archive* commit as the sole post-archive write mechanism. This diff's finishOrArchivedOnly lets `done --step retro` run in phase `archived`, and cmdDone's own commitBundle call (internal/cli/cmd_done.go:68, unchanged by this diff but exercised by the new path) takes an ordinary `retro done` commit after doneStepWork succeeds — confirmed by TestDoneRetroAcceptedInArchivedPhase asserting `git log -1 --format=%s` contains 'retro done', not 'archive'. The diff's own new doc comment (cmd_done.go:189-191) asserts 'design §7.5 step 5 already contemplates post-archive bundle writes', but step 5's actual text describes a different mechanism (sweeping dirty files into a second archive commit), not a distinct 'retro done' commit landing after archive — so the doc's 'last commit' invariant is left stale. plan.md's task 8 (docs/takt/lets-work-on-63/plan.md:89-97) scopes its edits and verify checks only to the step-3 markers, and the Risks section (plan.md:117-121) merely asserts (inaccurately, per the above) that step 5 'already contemplates' this, so no task actually updates step 5's text.

unfilledProseSlot converts b to a string twice: `i := strings.Index(string(b), marker)` and then `rest := string(b)[i:]`, each producing a fresh copy of the file contents rather than reusing a single conversion or bytes.Index.

doneRetro's `b, err := os.ReadFile(p)` (line 201) followed by `if err != nil { return fail(...) }` (lines 202-203) has no corresponding test that forces a read failure after fileNonEmpty succeeds (e.g. via os.Chmod on retro.md) — grepping the finish_test.go retro.md usages and the repo's Chmod-based failure tests shows none targets retro.md's ReadFile in doneRetro. The same untested-error-path shape exists in doneGoals's `os.ReadFile` (cmd_done.go:159-161), supporting the claim this is a pre-existing convention, not a new regression.

unfilledProseSlot's `j < 0` branch (`return rest, true`, returning the entire tail of the file when no closing `-->` is found) has no test — the only prose-slot test, TestDoneRetroRefusesUnfilledProseSlot, writes a marker with a proper closing `-->` (`<!-- prose: lessons for the next run -->`), and a repo-wide grep for `prose:` in internal/cli finds no other test constructing an unterminated marker.

The sentence 'Both refuse in the one shape finishOrArchivedOnly also uses for `done --step retro`, so a session learns it once' omits the relative pronoun 'that' before 'finishOrArchivedOnly', which is a standard reduced-relative-clause construction, not a grammatical defect — the same terse style (dropping 'that'/'which') appears throughout this exact file and diff, e.g. 'a retro found wanting months later must be redoable' two lines below at finishOrArchivedOnly's own doc comment, and 'a retrospective row 22 has not asked for yet' in cmd_done.go's doneRetro comment. The meaning parses unambiguously once read in full context.

finishOrArchivedOnly hardcodes `st.Phase == bundle.PhaseFinish || st.Phase == bundle.PhaseArchived` (cmd_verify.go:65), and cmd_status.go independently encodes the identical two-clause predicate `if st.Phase == bundle.PhaseFinish || st.Phase == bundle.PhaseArchived {` to decide whether to populate info.Finish — the diff adds a second, independent copy of this exact boolean rather than factoring it into one shared predicate used by both.
